raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Adds `docs/fe-oss-apis/api_conventions.md`, naming rules for **new** public op APIs (names added to `test/python/api_index/api_index.txt`). The graph API is out of scope. Existing names are unchanged; renames belong to the API pruning plan.

Pattern: `cudnn.<op_name>_<forward|backward>` for PyTorch, `cudnn.<op_name>_jax_<forward|backward>` for JAX, and `cudnn.<op_name>_standalone_<forward|backward>` for framework-free APIs that take raw device pointers and a stream. Each is a function exported from the top-level `cudnn` package.

Rules:
1. Functions only. Exported op classes such as `GroupedGemmSwigluSm100` are legacy.
2. No `wrapper` in names.
3. Spell out `forward` / `backward`; every op has a direction.
4. No architecture or implementation tokens (`sm100`, `dsl`, `frost`, ...); dispatch happens inside the function.
5. No op namespaces (`cudnn.torch`, `cudnn.jax`, `cudnn.gemm`); a JAX variant is marked by `_jax` in the name.

The doc is linked from the FE-OSS overview and Fern nav. The contributor guides (`AGENTS.md`, `python/cudnn/AGENTS.md`, `python/cudnn/README.md`, and the cutedsl integration skill) now describe new op APIs as public functions: what to validate, compile-once reuse, outputs, and stream handling.

**Codex bot review · model: `gpt-6-astra`**

Reviewed `e8a95bf20e51` against base `411012aa520d`.

Thank you for your contribution! The new-only naming policy is coherent: stable top-level functions, explicit direction/framework variants, internal architecture dispatch, and no rename of existing exports in this change. No approval-blocking issue found. One nonblocking correction is needed in the newly generalized JAX return-value guidance.

**[P2] Do not require an unregistered TupleDict as a JAX function result** ([source](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/e8a95bf20e511b99da0802e07f0b847fe3980e4e/python/cudnn/AGENTS.md#L686))

This rule now explicitly requires `<op>_jax_<direction>` functions to return TupleDict. The current TupleDict is an unregistered dict subclass, so returning it directly from a jax.jit-wrapped function raises TypeError rather than returning the op outputs. I reproduced this on CPU using the exact class definition from this head: `jax.jit(lambda x: TupleDict(output=x + 1))(1)` is rejected as an invalid JAX output type, while the plain-dict control passes. Please scope TupleDict guidance to the applicable tensor convenience APIs and require JAX-compatible pytrees for JAX results, or explicitly require a correctly registered return container. Apply the same qualification to the integration recipe. This is a documentation-contract correction; this PR itself does not change runtime exports.

Evidence: Source inspection found no TupleDict pytree registration. Exact-class CPU probe with JAX 0.11.2 reproduced the output-type rejection; a built-in dict control returned the expected value. Attribution: The changed public function contract explicitly extends the previous wrapper return convention to JAX APIs.

Validation: Reviewed all eight changed documentation/contributor-guide files and checked the new-only scope against existing exports and retained runtime rules. Parsed the modified Fern navigation YAML and verified the new overview/navigation target exists; git diff --check passed. Ran a CPU-only JAX return-container probe with the exact TupleDict class definition and a passing built-in dict control.

Limitations: No executable implementation or API-index change in this diff; GPU correctness/performance runs and a new GPU CI pipeline were not warranted. The JAX probe validates the documented return-container requirement, not a complete new GPU operation.

Approved: no P0 or high-risk P1 found. Remaining findings stay with the owner; merge timing stays with the owner.

+# Python API Naming Conventions
+
+These rules apply to every **new** public op API: any op name added to
+`test/python/api_index/api_index.txt`. The graph API (`cudnn.pygraph` and its
+enums) is out of scope. Existing names keep working; renaming them is part of
+the API pruning plan, not this document.
+
+## Name pattern
+
+```
+cudnn.<op_name>_<direction>               # PyTorch
+cudnn.<op_name>_jax_<direction>           # JAX
+cudnn.<op_name>_standalone_<direction>    # no framework
+```
+
+- `<op_name>`: the operation in snake_case, such as `grouped_gemm_swiglu` or `sdpa`.
+- `jax`: marks the JAX variant. The PyTorch variant has no framework token.
+- `standalone`: marks the framework-free variant, which takes raw device
+  pointers and a stream instead of framework tensors.
+- `<direction>`: `forward` or `backward`. Every op has a direction, including an
+  op without a backward.
+
+Each name is a function exported from the top-level `cudnn` package.
+
+## Rules
+
+1. **Functions only.** Do not export op classes. Exported op classes such as
+   `GroupedGemmSwigluSm100` are legacy.
+2. **No `wrapper` in names.** The function is the framework op; `wrapper` adds
+   nothing.
+3. **Spell out the direction.** Use `forward` / `backward`, never `fwd` / `bwd`.
+4. **Keep implementation details out of names.** Do not add an architecture
+   (`sm90`, `sm100`, ...) or an implementation technology (`dsl`, `cutedsl`,
+   `frost`, `triton`, ...). The function dispatches internally and raises a
+   clear error for an unsupported configuration.
+5. **No namespaces for ops.** Do not add op APIs under `cudnn.torch`,
+   `cudnn.jax`, or an op package such as `cudnn.gemm`; a JAX variant is marked
+   by `_jax` in the name. Existing exports keep working until the API pruning
+   plan retires them.
+
+## Examples
+
+| Existing name | New API name |
+| --- | --- |
+| `cudnn.gemm.cutedsl.grouped.grouped_gemm_swiglu_wrapper_sm100` | `cudnn.grouped_gemm_swiglu_forward` |
+| `cudnn.gemm.cutedsl.grouped.GroupedGemmSwigluSm100` | none; use `cudnn.grouped_gemm_swiglu_forward` |
+| `cudnn.gemm.cutedsl.grouped.grouped_gemm_glu_jax_sm100` | `cudnn.grouped_gemm_glu_jax_forward` |
+| `cudnn.sdpa.fwd.sdpa_fwd_wrapper_dsl_sm100` | `cudnn.sdpa_forward` |
+| `cudnn.deepseek_sparse_attention.sparse_attention_backward_wrapper` | `cudnn.sparse_attention_backward` |
+| `cudnn.flex_attention.FlexAttentionBwd` | `cudnn.flex_attention_backward` |
+| `cudnn.rmsnorm_rht_amax.rmsnorm_rht_amax_wrapper_sm100` | `cudnn.rmsnorm_rht_amax_forward` |
+| `cudnn.torch.block_sparse_attention_forward` | `cudnn.block_sparse_attention_forward` |
+| `cudnn.jax.block_sparse_attention_forward` | `cudnn.block_sparse_attention_jax_forward` |
+| `cudnn.jax.kimi_delta_attention_fwd` | `cudnn.kimi_delta_attention_jax_forward` |
+| `cudnn.causal_conv1d_forward` (raw pointers) | `cudnn.causal_conv1d_standalone_forward` |

**Codex bot review · model: `gpt-6-astra`**

Reviewed `e8a95bf20e51` against base `411012aa520d`.

Thank you for your contribution! The new-only naming policy is coherent: stable top-level functions, explicit direction/framework variants, internal architecture dispatch, and no rename of existing exports in this change. No approval-blocking issue found. One nonblocking correction is needed in the newly generalized JAX return-value guidance.

**[P2] Do not require an unregistered TupleDict as a JAX function result** ([source](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/e8a95bf20e511b99da0802e07f0b847fe3980e4e/python/cudnn/AGENTS.md#L686))

This rule now explicitly requires `<op>_jax_<direction>` functions to return TupleDict. The current TupleDict is an unregistered dict subclass, so returning it directly from a jax.jit-wrapped function raises TypeError rather than returning the op outputs. I reproduced this on CPU using the exact class definition from this head: `jax.jit(lambda x: TupleDict(output=x + 1))(1)` is rejected as an invalid JAX output type, while the plain-dict control passes. Please scope TupleDict guidance to the applicable tensor convenience APIs and require JAX-compatible pytrees for JAX results, or explicitly require a correctly registered return container. Apply the same qualification to the integration recipe. This is a documentation-contract correction; this PR itself does not change runtime exports.

Evidence: Source inspection found no TupleDict pytree registration. Exact-class CPU probe with JAX 0.11.2 reproduced the output-type rejection; a built-in dict control returned the expected value. Attribution: The changed public function contract explicitly extends the previous wrapper return convention to JAX APIs.

Validation: Reviewed all eight changed documentation/contributor-guide files and checked the new-only scope against existing exports and retained runtime rules. Parsed the modified Fern navigation YAML and verified the new overview/navigation target exists; git diff --check passed. Ran a CPU-only JAX return-container probe with the exact TupleDict class definition and a passing built-in dict control.

Limitations: No executable implementation or API-index change in this diff; GPU correctness/performance runs and a new GPU CI pipeline were not warranted. The JAX probe validates the documented return-container requirement, not a complete new GPU operation.

Approved: no P0 or high-risk P1 found. Remaining findings stay with the owner; merge timing stays with the owner.
